data.title: Mud Season
data.rumour: Hal Mayhew pulled something out of the mud on Harbor Green that went missing at the Harvest Fair.
about: A March story. Pulling his tent stakes out of the thawing Green, Hal found a padlocked Grange cash box: the 50/50 money that went missing on Harvest Fair night, which got treasurer Clyde Blaisdell blamed and made him quit (§{halCashBox}). Inside are $240, the raffle stubs, and Clyde's reading glasses.

On the muddy Green (§{mudGreen}) Clyde explains that he buried the box under a stake to keep it safe in the storm, couldn't find it after the stakes were moved, and found it easier to be the man who took it than the man who lost it. Take it to the Grange so the 50/50 is drawn at last and Clyde is asked back (The Draw), give it to Clyde to walk in himself (His Own Hands), or keep the money, which costs heat and reputation (Finders Keepers).
data.notes: months: [6]: the thaw, when the Green gives back what October left in it.

fairCashBox.name: A muddy padlocked cash box
tells: Green tin, padlocked, caked in Harbor Green. Stencilled on the lid: GRANGE No. 214.

tells.text: It rattles like coins and rustles like paper. Somebody wrapped the paper in a bread bag first.

halCashBox.title: Hal brings in a cash box from the mud

text: Mud season. The Green's soup. I lent the Grange forty tent stakes for the Harvest Fair and they froze in. I went out this morning with a bar to get them back.
Stake thirty-one came up with this on the end of it. Green tin box, padlocked. GRANGE No. 214. You know what that is. Everybody over fifty in this town knows what that is.
It's the 50/50 from fair night. It went missing in the thunderstorm, before the draw. They blamed Clyde Blaisdell. He'd been treasurer twenty years. He quit the Grange that week.
I don't want it in my store. It's got a padlock and it's got a smell. Twenty dollars, and you have the bolt cutters.

then.text: Then it goes to Captain Barrow, and Clyde gets his name in the paper again. Wrong paper, maybe. It's the only paper.

steps.narrate: The padlock gives on the second go. Inside, wrapped in a bread bag: two hundred and forty dollars in fives and ones, a roll of raffle stubs, and a pair of reading glasses with one arm mended with tape.

text: Those are Clyde's glasses. He wore them on a string. He lost them that night, he said. Lost them. Huh.
He walks his dog on the Green at noon. Every day, mud or no mud. You could ask him. I couldn't. I'd say the wrong thing. I sell hammers.

mudGreen.title: Clyde Blaisdell walks his dog on the Green

steps.narrate: Harbor Green at noon in mud season: duckboards across the paths, snowbanks gone gray and lacy, and forty holes in a ring where the fair tent stood. A man in a cap is walking a very old dog around them.

then.text: Hal says you had the box. Had. Well. It's been out of my hands since October. It can stay out.

steps.narrate: You hold up the reading glasses. He stops. The dog stops.

text: The tent came down in the storm. Everybody ran. I had the box under my arm and four hundred people in the dark and I thought, I'll put it where nobody will look. Under my own stake. By the ticket table. Dig it up at dawn.

At dawn they'd pulled half the stakes and moved the rest, and then the frost came, and I couldn't find it. I dug six holes. I told the Grange. They looked at me the way you look at a man who's dug six holes.
So I stopped telling them. It's easier to be the man who took it than the man who lost it. Nobody argues with you.

choose.label: Take the box to the Grange and have them draw the 50/50 at last

narrate: Saturday's bean supper at the Grange. The 50/50 is drawn five months late, out of a mixing bowl. The winning ticket belongs to a girl of ten, who screams.
Somebody asks Clyde Blaisdell to read out the treasurer's report. He says he hasn't got one. They ask him to do one for next month. He puts his glasses on.

choose.label: Give the box to Clyde, to take in himself

then.text: Myself. Yes. I'll walk it in. In the front door, at the supper, with the dog. Let them look.

then.narrate: He tucks the box under his arm exactly the way he must have on fair night, and walks off across the duckboards, the dog behind him.

choose.label: Keep the money. Nobody knows you opened it

then.why: Kept the Grange 50/50 money from the Harvest Fair

then.text: Kept it. Then it's still lost, and I'm still the man who lost it. That's all right. I'm used to him.

then.narrate: He walks on round the ring of holes. The dog looks back at you once, for quite a long time.

errands.title: Clyde Blaisdell walks his dog on the Green

epilogue.line: Clyde Blaisdell is treasurer of the Grange again. He reads the report every month with his glasses on a string, and the ten-year-old who won the 50/50 sells tickets now.
Clyde Blaisdell walked the 50/50 box into the Grange bean supper himself, with his dog. Nobody said anything. Then everybody did.
The Grange's 50/50 from the Harvest Fair is still missing, officially. Hal Mayhew measures your nails very carefully these days.

rumour: Mud season. Sold forty pairs of boots this week and a man asked for a canoe. The Green is soup.
I lent the Grange my tent stakes for the fair. They're still out there, frozen in. I'm going out with a bar. If I find anything else, I'll let you know.

react.grange: Clyde's back at the Grange. He came in for a new pair of glasses cord. I gave it him free. Don't tell anybody I give things free.
react.clyde: Clyde walked that box in himself. I was at the supper. I've never heard a room go that quiet over beans.
react.kept: That box had money in it. I didn't open it. I know what tin sounds like with money in it. I sell tin.
